To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the measurement uncertainty of amperometric sensors is mainly influenced by the properties of the sensor, the properties of the measured sample, measurement conditions, the method of calibration, the method of measurement, and the method of uncertainty evaluation.
the main uncertainty sources are: (a) the electrode surface, (b) the sample composition, (c) the measurement conditions, (d) the measurement procedure and (e) the calibration procedure.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the measurement uncertainty estimation in electrochemical sensors.
the development, application, and validation of amperometric sensors.
the development and application of amperometric sensors for the detection and determination of various compounds in liquid and gas samples.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the uncertainty of amperometric sensors depends on the principles of their operation, the measurement conditions and the properties of the measured sample.
the measurement uncertainty of an amperometric sensor is a function of the sensor type, the principles of operation, the measurement conditions and the properties of the sample to be analyzed.
the uncertainty of amperometric sensors can be reduced by using the most appropriate measurement conditions and by minimizing the influence of the main uncertainty sources.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the uncertainty estimation in am perometric sensors is a challenging task, but the obtained results are expected to be of great benefit to both the users and manufacturers of the sensors, as well as the researchers in the field.
measurement uncertainty evaluation is an important step in the process of making measurement results more accurate and reliable.

the measurement uncertainty in amperometric gas-phase measurements is dominated by the uncertainty of the calibration factor and the uncertainty of the sample flow rate, whereas in liquid-phase measurements it is dominated by the calibration factor, the sample flow rate and the electrode surface.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the measurement uncertainties of amperometric sensors can be evaluated by the two major approaches and the results can be compared.
the uncertainty of amperometric sensors can be evaluated with a high degree of accuracy and confidence.
the measurement uncertainty in amperometric measurements is dominated by the reproducibility of the measurements and the uncertainty of the calibration.
